metadata.name: Output CSV (HK) line items
changes: absorbed all 462 rulebook concepts: 454 projected, 8 merged with configured assembly, 13 configurator-only parts
declaration order follows the rulebook, so ties decided by order agree

the eight output lines no longer name a service implementer. The five derivation services were REMOVED - deprec_impairment (~208 enumerated entries), contingent_liabilities (~172, its NUMBER only; its narrative disclosure survives), secur_fincl_assets (~91), related_party_receivables (~73), sales_revenues (~18): ~562 hand-enumerated note titles, row captions and formula variants in all. `implemented_by` is therefore deleted from all eight and every figure must now come from configuration. The six cascade-less lines - is_pl__sales_revenues, bs_ca__secur_and_other_fincl_assets_cp, bs_nca__secur_and_other_fincl_assets_ltp, bs_nca__due_from_related_parties_ltp, bs_ca__other_receivables_cp, notes__contingent_liabilities - are now `extracted`, since a `derived` line with neither a cascade nor an implementer is refused by LineItemDef; the two depreciation lines stay `derived` on their own cascades (P1-P5 and COS_P1/COS_P2). Cells these services used to fill go blank until the configuration reads them off a caption - that is the intended outcome, so do not reinstate a service name here. Mirrored in output_csv_hk_line_items_configured.json, which is the assembly half of this file

authored expected_components prose on the 11 exclusive_residual buckets (3-4 caption phrases each, 37 in total): the payload block services.mapping._residual_expectations publishes as "captions_with_no_dedicated_concept" was empty on every statement, so an empty canonical_key was never a licensed answer. Each phrase was checked against all 462 concepts' labels and aliases in its own section; hkfrs_hk_china_ontology.json's wording was NOT copied - "Bank overdrafts", "Pension surplus", "Right-of-use assets", "Biological assets", "Contract liabilities", "Bills receivable", "Merger reserve", "Deposits paid for acquisition of land", "Donations" and "Sales taxes and surcharges" all have dedicated concepts here and would have routed real money into a sweep
breaking_changes: the set is now 475 definitions, not 21
metadata.vocabulary_note: INERT ON THE DEFAULT ENGINE. The six scoping blocks in `vocabulary` (section_banners 18, umbrella_banners 1, scope_tokens 12, statement_prefixes 4, statement_spellings 1, exclusive_vocabularies 1 = 37 declarations) are consulted only by services/line_item_matching.Vocabulary, reached only under extraction.mapping_engine = "line_items"; config.py ships "ontology" and config.toml names the setting nowhere, so on the shipped default the answers come from services/mapping's module constants, which 49 call sites across 12 modules read with no set in hand. 16 of the 37 (scope_tokens, statement_prefixes) are a test-pinned mirror of those constants (tests/test_buckets_vocabulary.py). Two exceptions: section_banners is walked on every load by MappingVocabulary.refuse_shadowed_banners, a self-consistency refusal rather than a section-scoping read, and caption_characters (not one of the six) is installed into services/mapping at startup by services/line_item_config, so it is live on both engines.

umbrella_banners.note: IFRS statements print EQUITY AND LIABILITIES above the Equity, Non-current and Current sub-banners; reading it as equity would refuse every liability line item beneath it.

exclusive_vocabularies.note: IAS 7 divides cash flows into exactly three activities and a statement labels each subtotal with its own, so naming one rules out the others.

normalisation.note: Applied to every candidate row label and every alias before comparison. Folding is what allows a single Chinese alias to cover both scripts.
pipeline: Traditional to Simplified fold (OpenCC t2s) applied to BOTH sides of the comparison, so 銷售成本 and 销售成本 collapse to one key.
Full-width to half-width punctuation; map ╱ ／ ⁄ to /; map （） to (); map 、 to , .
Strip footnote and note markers: trailing digits in parentheses, superscripts, '(note 12)', '附註12', '(附注12)'.
Strip trailing colons and dashes used to introduce sub-captions ('Share of profits and losses of:').
Strip inline unit and currency annotations: "RMB'000", '人民幣千元', '(unaudited)', '（未經審核）'.
Collapse internal whitespace to a single space; strip zero-width characters and soft hyphens.
Join a wrapped caption to its continuation line before matching, then also retain the bare fragment as a fallback candidate.
normalisation.wrapped_caption_rule: On a bilingual HKEX statement a caption printed across two physical lines ('TOTAL COMPREHENSIVE' / '年內全面虧損總額' / 'LOSS FOR THE YEAR') must be reassembled from the value row upward before matching. Match the reassembled string first; only if that fails may the bare fragment be used, and then only against concepts whose include criteria explicitly admit the fragment.

binding.note: Precedence is section-first. A concept can only claim a row printed inside one of its section_scope values.
order: 1. Resolve the statement (balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / cash_flow) from the page or table caption.

2. Resolve the printed section from the nearest preceding section header. If no header is resolvable, the row is unbound: route to review, never guess a section. (A row WITH a resolved section that no concept claims is not unbound — it is swept into that section's residual; see unbound_row_policy.)
3. Restrict the candidate concept set to concepts whose section_scope contains the resolved section.
4. Rule tier: exact normalised alias, then regex_hints, in descending match_priority. Any exclude_hints hit is a hard veto, not a score penalty.
5. Semantic tier over the restricted set only, using definition + include + exclude. Never over the full ontology.
6. Tie between concepts listed in each other's confusable_with: resolve with section_disambiguation; if still tied, emit both as candidates and route to review. Never pick by declaration order.
7. Residual sweep (see residual_framework) runs last, over rows no dedicated concept claimed.
8. Reconcile the section against its reported subtotal.
binding.unbound_row_policy: Route an unclaimed face value only to the residual for its resolved printed section. Never borrow a neighbouring concept or cross a section. After all mapping and gap-closing opportunities, the engine-level face_mapping_contract gives any remaining face value a unique engine_unclassified_face key outside the ontology/template namespaces. This keeps the row stored and reviewable without feeding it into an unrelated calculation. Verified non-additive aggregates replaced by mapped components remain evidence-only.
binding.match_priority: Integer 0-99, higher evaluated first. Long specific captions rank above short generic ones so 'Total assets less current liabilities' cannot be pre-empted by 'Total current liabilities' on token overlap. Residuals are 0 and unreachable by matching.

prompt: Map each caption to the concept whose definition and criteria best match what the caption REPRESENTS. Rely on financial meaning, not string similarity or shared words. Respect the exclusion criteria and the confusable-with warnings.

sign_convention.stored_value: The reported value after paren-to-negative conversion.
sign_convention.expenses_and_outflows: Stored NEGATIVE. This is required by the template: pl_gross_profit = sum(revenue, cost_of_goods_sold) and pl_profit_before_exceptional_items_and_tax = sum(total_income, total_operating_cost, total_non_operating_expense) only hold if expense concepts carry a negative sign.
sign_convention.unsigned_source: Where a filing prints expenses as unsigned positives in a by-nature list, negate on load and set sign_normalised: true on the fact so the transformation is auditable.
sign_convention.either: Subtotals, working-capital movements, fair-value changes, share of results, OCI and net cash flows are sign-indeterminate. Retain the reported sign; never coerce.
sign_convention.validation: A concept whose sign_convention is positive_expected or negative_expected but whose loaded value carries the opposite sign is a review trigger, not an auto-correction.

global_rules.face_only_default: Concepts default to face_only: true. Notes are evidence for a face amount, never an independent source of one, unless note_use is decomposition_allowed.
global_rules.duplicate_fact_rule: The same economic fact on the face and in a note is one fact with multiple evidence references, not two additive values. This also applies to two face captions that report the same amount (see equivalence blocks).
parent_child_allocation: Never load a gross parent and its separately mapped children additively.
Residual = reported parent minus confirmed included children.
Subtract only on explicit inclusion wording, hierarchy, reconciliation or arithmetic support.
If containment is uncertain, retain the parent as evidence and route to review.
global_rules.no_fabricated_split: Never invent a decomposition. Where only a combined figure is reported, load the combined concept and leave the children empty. The one exception is a concept declaring sole_component_of: assigning a whole undifferentiated figure to a single child divides nothing, and it is refused as soon as any sibling child is evidenced on the face or in the subtotal's own note.
global_rules.totals_policy: Compute totals from mutually exclusive concept outputs. Use reported totals only for validation, never as an input to the components.

scope_selection.note: Absent from v1 and a common cause of silent mis-loads on HKEX filings.

entity_scope.rule: Where a statement prints Group and Company columns side by side, take the Group (consolidated) column. Record entity_scope on every fact. Never mix columns within one statement.
company_only_markers: Presence of bs_non_current_assets__investments_in_subsidiaries on the face is strong evidence the column is company-only, since consolidation eliminates it.

period_selection.rule: Identify the current period from the column heading date, not from column position; HKEX filings are not consistently current-first. Load comparatives only into the comparative period slot.
period_selection.restatement_rule: Where a comparative column is labelled restated / 重列 / 經重列, load it as the comparative and set restated: true. Do not overwrite a previously loaded original comparative; keep both with a restatement flag.

units_and_currency.rule: Resolve currency and scale from the statement header, not the cover page, and re-resolve per statement. Persist unit on every fact; never normalise scale silently.
units_and_currency.conflict: If header scale and a printed subtotal are inconsistent by a factor of 1,000, trust neither: route the statement to review.

scope_selection.column_guard: Every fact carries the resolved (entity_scope, period, currency, unit). Two facts for the same canonical_key that differ on any of these are distinct facts, not duplicates.

residual_framework.note: One definition governing the 11 output-template subsection residuals. Each uses an existing template line; no template row is added.

sweep.runs: after all dedicated concepts in the section have been resolved, before section reconciliation
sweep.candidate_set: every printed value row on the FACE of the statement whose resolved section equals the residual's single section_scope value
eligibility: The row printed a value for the selected entity_scope, period, currency and unit.
No dedicated concept whose section_scope contains this section claimed the row.
The row is not a section subtotal, statement total, section header, attribution caption, per-share figure, narrative row, note-reference-only row or truncated caption.
The row was printed INSIDE this section. A row printed in any other section is ineligible however similar its wording — there is no cross-section rescue.

The row's sign agrees with the section's sign_convention, where the section states one. A row signed against its section is evidence the SECTION is wrong, not the amount, so it goes to review rather than into the bucket — a cost swept into income moves the income subtotal and every total below it.
sweep.plug_behaviour: forbidden — the residual is never computed as (reported subtotal − mapped children)
sweep.literal_others_caption: A row captioned 'Others' / '其他' is simply one unmapped face row and sweeps in as a single component. It gets no privileged treatment and no dedicated concept.

itemisation.rule: The residual's value is the arithmetic sum of its components. Original labels and signs are always retained; a swept row is never relabelled to 'Others'.

reconciliation.identity: reported_section_subtotal − Σ(dedicated concepts in section) − Σ(residual components) = 0
reconciliation.tolerance: one rounding unit per contributing row
reconciliation.on_failure: Emit an unallocated_gap fact carrying the difference and route the section to review. Never adjust the residual, and never adjust a dedicated concept, to close the gap.
reconciliation.sections_without_reported_subtotal: If the section prints no subtotal, the residual is still itemised but is flagged unreconciled and carries lower confidence.

review_triggers: any single component exceeds 2% of |reported section subtotal|
a component label scored at or above the semantic threshold against a dedicated concept but was vetoed by exclude_hints
residual sign is opposite to the section's sign_convention
the section reconciliation emitted an unallocated_gap
prohibitions: Never populated by alias, regex or embedding match.
Never carries a value with no itemised components.
Never absorbs a row a dedicated concept could have claimed but was not tested for — all dedicated concepts in the section must be evaluated first.
Never spans sections, statements, periods, entity scopes or units.

cascade.note: Spec 4.2, Candidate 1: 'Find_1 = SUM(Find_1_components excluding entrusted loans)', the unique net related-party balances identified on the balance sheet and in statement-linked disclosures. One child feeds it, so the term is required. Declared first because the spec enumerates Find 1 first (sections 2, 4.2 and 7); note that the spec's actual selection rule is MAX_VALID(Find 1, Find 2, Find 3), not first-available, so this rung's precedence is the spec's declaration order rather than a claim that the face is the best measurement. No deduction: the shared veto already excludes entrusted loans (3.4), and where a face figure bundles an inseparable entrusted loan 3.4 requires the candidate be left not computable rather than netted.

Spec 4.3, Candidate 2: 'Find_2 = SUM(Find_2_components excluding entrusted loans)', the unique net related-party balances in the specified receivable notes. The four notes are mutually exclusive receivable classes — in PRC presentation the current portion is reclassified out of 长期应收款 — so summing them counts each underlying receivable once (3.5). Every term is any_of because the spec sums whatever subset the filing discloses and a missing note is not a failure (3.6: return null, never zero-fill). refuse_negative is set because this rung computes a receivable balance; a negative would mean the inputs did not mean what the rung assumed.

Spec 4.4, Candidate 3, read by receivable class: the related-party note's own rows for 其他应收款, 一年内到期的长期应收款, 长期应收款 and 发放贷款及垫款 / 贷款及垫款, which is the order 4.4's 'Search line items' list gives. Placed ahead of the two aggregate readings of the same note because 3.5 forbids adding a subtotal to its components — where the note gives a class breakdown, the breakdown is the component-level measurement and the umbrella line is the subtotal, so the two are alternatives and never both fire. No deduction needed: the shared veto keeps entrusted loans out of these class rows.

Spec 4.4, Candidate 3, read by counterparty type: the same note's per-party rows (母公司, 子公司, 联营企业, 合营企业, 受同一控制方控制的企业, 其他关联方, and the HK associates / joint ventures / fellow subsidiaries / directors forms). A separate rung from 3A rather than a summed sibling, because the class view and the counterparty view of one note describe the SAME underlying receivables from two angles — 3.5: 'If the same related-party balance appears under two source notes but represents the same underlying receivable, retain one value within that candidate.' Also no deduction, for the same reason as 3A.

Spec 4.4, Candidate 3, read as the note's single umbrella related-party receivable line, used when the filing gives one figure and no breakdown. Ranked below 3A and 3B because it is the coarsest of the three readings of this note. This is the first rung whose base can bundle entrusted loans, so sub__rp_note_entrusted_loans enters as an adjustment with sign -1: 3.4 requires entrusted loans out of every related-party calculation, and deducting a separately disclosed 委托贷款 row from a bundled total is precisely the 'separation' 3.4 contemplates. The deduction is an adjustment, not a base — on its own it would leave the rung with nothing to deduct from — and refuse_negative discards the rung if the disclosed entrusted loans exceed the umbrella figure, which would prove the two did not refer to the same pool.

Spec 4.4 also lists 应收关联方款项 as a related-party note heading in its own right; this rung reads that dedicated 'Amounts due from related companies' note and takes only its non-current-tenor rows, which is what the bs_nca parent means. Last because it is the fallback the parent's definition describes for a filing with no matching Chinese note headings — an English-language HK filing. Same entrusted-loan adjustment as 3C, for the same reason: the base is a single bundled tenor figure. Reviewer check against the quoted formula: these six rungs are Find_1, Find_2, and Find_3 in its four readings — alternatives, never summed (4.5: 'Do not add Find_1, Find_2, and Find_3'), which is why the parent rolls up as alternatives; the spec's MAX_VALID selection is approximated by this declared precedence order.

cascade.note: Primary. Find_1_LTP from the rows the in-scope notes themselves classify as non-current, less Find_2_LTP, plus the CP carry-forward. This rung leads because spec 6.1 admits only amounts classified under Non-current Assets, so where a note analyses its own total into current and non-current that analysis IS the figure. The three deductions are adjustments at sign -1 and are optional: spec 6.3 lets Find_2_LTP be zero when the notes were found and no component is included in their totals, and a deduction can never make this rung resolvable on its own. The last term is the CP carry-forward: spec 6.4 - 'LTP_candidate = LTP_base + CP_negative_carryforward_to_LTP'. It is zero or negative, so sign +1 ADDS it and it reduces LTP by the Level 3 amount CP could not absorb; role adjustment keeps a carry-forward from resolving this rung on its own, since there would be nothing to add it to. The evaluator must hand over the CARRY-FORWARD (zero, or the negative CP candidate) - not the clamped CP output, which spec 5.4 sets to zero in exactly the case where the carry-forward is non-zero. refuse_negative is spec 6.4's 'LTP_final = LTP_base if LTP_candidate < 0': a negative candidate is skipped and LTP_P2, the same Find_1 source without the carry-forward, supplies LTP_base.  [The spec's CP negative carry-forward term is OMITTED: it is min(CP_candidate, 0) and the only available reference holds CP_final, which the spec clamps to >= 0. Adding that would fold the whole current figure into this line. This rung therefore computes the spec's LTP_base.]

LTP_base from the same rows, with no carry-forward applied - 'LTP_base = Find_1_LTP - Find_2_LTP'. Both of the spec's escape hatches land here: the carry-forward is unavailable (MISSING_CP_CARRYFORWARD_TO_LTP), or applying it made the candidate negative and LTP_P1 was refused (NEGATIVE_LTP_ADJUSTMENT_REVERSED - 'when applying the negative CP carry-forward would make LTP negative, do not apply the carry-forward. Use the unadjusted LTP_base as the final LTP value'). refuse_negative because LTP is a carrying amount: a negative result would mean the deductions were not the components this rung assumed.

The same arithmetic where the in-scope notes are wholly non-current and print a total rather than a current/non-current split, so Find_1_LTP is 'SUM(unique note_total across all identified Non-current Asset notes)'. The eight note children are any_of because that SUM takes whatever subset of the 6.1 dictionary a filing happens to disclose, and each of them owns one note heading, so no note total is added twice. Deductions and the CP carry-forward behave exactly as in LTP_P1, including refuse_negative for 6.4's reversal rule, which drops to LTP_P4.  [The spec's CP negative carry-forward term is OMITTED: it is min(CP_candidate, 0) and the only available reference holds CP_final, which the spec clamps to >= 0. Adding that would fold the whole current figure into this line. This rung therefore computes the spec's LTP_base.]

LTP_base for the note-total source: the same eight notes less Find_2_LTP, with no carry-forward - reached when the carry-forward is unavailable (MISSING_CP_CARRYFORWARD_TO_LTP) or when applying it turned LTP_P3 negative (NEGATIVE_LTP_ADJUSTMENT_REVERSED). refuse_negative because LTP is a carrying amount.

cascade.note: Spec 5.4 primary formula, verbatim: CP_candidate = Find_1_CP - Find_2_CP - Find_3_CP. Find_1_CP is 'SUM(unique note_total across all identified Current Asset notes)', so each of the six note-total children is any_of — a filing that prints only the FVTPL and money-market notes still sums those two, and none of the six is individually required. The non-current split child is an adjustment because spec 5.1 and spec 8 admit only current-classified amounts, and it can only ever reduce a total another child already read. The two Find_2_CP components are adjustments too: spec 5.3 allows Find_2_CP to be zero when the notes were found and neither component is inside their totals, so neither may make this rung resolve. Find_3_CP is the one term declared required with sign -1: the primary formula cannot be evaluated without the Level 3 total, and spec 5.4 forbids treating a missing Level 3 disclosure as zero, so this rung must die when the fair-value-hierarchy note is absent and hand over to CP_P2. refuse_negative is deliberately false here, and this is the one place in the family where a negative result is not evidence of a mis-read: spec 5.4 requires the negative candidate to be preserved — 'If CP_candidate is negative, do not replace the negative candidate with Find_1_CP - Find_2_CP', the reported CP output is zero and the original negative candidate carries forward to LTP. Refusing the negative here would send the engine down to CP_P2, which computes exactly the Find_1_CP - Find_2_CP figure the spec prohibits.

Spec 5.4 'Missing Level 3', verbatim: 'IF the fair value hierarchy note or Level 3 value is not found: CP_final = Find_1_CP - Find_2_CP; CP_negative_carryforward_to_LTP = null; raise MISSING_LEVEL_3.' Identical to CP_P1 with the Level 3 term dropped, which is why it sits second: it is reachable only when CP_P1 died for want of the Level 3 total, never as an escape from a negative CP_P1 result. refuse_negative is true here, unlike CP_P1: with no Level 3 subtraction this rung is note totals less components proven to sit inside those totals, so a negative can only mean the deduction rows were not in fact part of the extracted totals — spec 3.3 and the DEDUCTION_NOT_PROVEN_INCLUDED / PARENT_COMPONENT_OVERLAP flags — and the rung should be skipped rather than reported.

cascade.note: The spec's primary formula: CP_Gross - CP_Related_Party_Deduction, with every gross component taken on the explicit net-carrying-amount basis (spec 3.2 preference 1). The five gross components are any_of because 5.2 says only add a component when the filing separately identifies it, so whatever subset was disclosed is still the sum. The five related-party legs are adjustments with sign -1: each is read from the SAME note that supplied its own gross component, which is what proves the amount is inside CP_Gross, and none of them can make this rung resolve on its own - a rung holding only a deduction has nothing to deduct it from. Deliberately five paired legs rather than one LTP total, because sections 2 and 5.3 forbid deducting the final Due from Related Parties(LTP) value: that total may include 长期应收款 and non-current loans and advances that lie outside this pool. refuse_negative is set because 5.4 says a negative candidate is a NEGATIVE_RESIDUAL, returned as null and never floored at zero.

The same formula, reached the second way the spec allows when the other-receivables note prints no explicit net carrying amount: spec 3.2 preference 2, closing balance less loss allowance or bad-debt provision. The gross closing balance is required, and the loss allowance is an adjustment with sign -1 - it is a negative row that belongs in the arithmetic, not in the veto list, and a filing that states its balance is already net or that no allowance applies still resolves this rung as gross less nothing. The other four components stay on their net-carrying-amount children and stay any_of, and the five related-party legs deduct exactly as in CP_P1. Second in order because the spec ranks the explicit net amount above the derived one; the first rung that resolves wins, so this fires only when CP_P1 found no explicit net figure. refuse_negative for the same NEGATIVE_RESIDUAL reason.

cascade.note: PRIORITY 1, the spec verbatim: 'P1 = 主营业务收入 reported on the face of the income statement.' One required term — the face either prints the 主营业务收入 / 主营业务 (Revenue / Turnover / Sales) row or it does not; there is nothing to sum and nothing to deduct. refuse_negative because sales revenue is a positive magnitude, and a negative here would mean a 成本 or 增减 column was read instead of 收入.

PRIORITY 2, the spec verbatim: 'P2 = 主营业务 revenue reported in the 营业收入 note.' Reached only when P1 resolved nothing, which is §5's first duplicate control: 'Do not add the amount from the face of the income statement to the amount in the note' — so this is a rung, not an addend. The note's four title spellings are all in the child; §3's column rule and §4's ban on the combined 营业收入 total are carried as row vetoes on the child, not as a deduction here.

The same Priority-2 disclosure under its own 主营业务收入 / 主营业务收支 heading. A SEPARATE RUNG, never an any_of sibling of P2: two notes restating one figure are alternatives, and summing them would be exactly the double count §5 prohibits.

The English/HK revenue note ('Revenue', 'Turnover', 'Revenue from contracts with customers', 營業額), for filings with no 主营业务 / 其他业务 split for §2 to read. Last of the directly-reported routes so a PRC filing resolves on 主营业务 before any translated caption is considered — §4 forbids substituting a total for the principal-operations figure.

Alternative RECONSTRUCTION from the PRODUCT axis, first of the four axis rungs because §5 enumerates 'product, industry, or geographic'. One axis per rung: the axes are alternative reconstructions of ONE revenue figure, not components of it, so combining two of them in a single rung would count the same revenue twice. The child reads the axis-qualified total only, never the product components.

Alternative reconstruction from the INDUSTRY / OPERATING-SEGMENT axis (主营业务分行业情况, or the IFRS segment note). Second in §5's own order. Its own rung, not an any_of sibling of P5 — an industry reconstruction and a product reconstruction of the same revenue must never be added.
Alternative reconstruction from the GEOGRAPHIC axis (主营业务分地区情况, geographical information). Third in §5's order, and again its own rung.

Alternative reconstruction from the SALES-CHANNEL axis. Last because the spec does not name this axis; it is offered only after every route the spec does name has failed. NOTE ON THE WHOLE CASCADE: no rung carries a term with sign -1. The spec contains no subtraction — §3's cost columns, §4's combined 营业收入 total and §5's product/industry/geographic components are all EXCLUSIONS, transcribed as row-caption vetoes on the children. Deriving 主营业务收入 as 'note total less 其他业务收入' would build the answer out of the very total §4 forbids using, so it is deliberately absent.

cascade.note: §6.1 primary. The four classified type totals — Letters_of_Credit_Total + Performance_Bonds_Total + Bank_Guarantees_Total + Corporate_Guarantees_Total — read from the dedicated contingent-liabilities / contingencies note (whose title pattern also matches the combined 承诺及或有事项 / Commitments and contingencies heading; capital and lease commitments are vetoed at row level). All four terms are any_of because a filing discloses whatever subset of the four it has, and the four children partition that note's rows by instrument qualifier in §5 priority order (LC vetoes nothing, PB vetoes LC, BG vetoes LC+PB, corporate vetoes LC+PB+BG), so summing them cannot count one row twice. refuse_negative: this rung computes an exposure, so a negative result means the rows were not what it assumed.

§3's amount selection. The dedicated external-guarantee note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), at the AMOUNT UTILISED — the outstanding guarantee balance, "the most specific outstanding exposure". This is a RUNG, not a term of CL_P1: §6.4 says the same guarantee is repeated across 或有负债 and 对外担保 and must be treated as one item, so the two notes are alternative sources of a single figure and adding them would double count. refuse_negative: an outstanding exposure cannot be negative.

§3 fallback, and the place where AMOUNT GUARANTEED is kept apart from AMOUNT UTILISED. The same external-guarantee note read at the contracted amount guaranteed, used only when the note prints no outstanding balance — never added to CL_P2's figure, because the two are different amounts for one exposure. Guarantees released or repaid in the period (已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额) are deducted: the contracted amount still contains them and §3 forbids either as the exposure figure. The deduction is role adjustment with sign -1, so it can never make this rung resolve on its own — a released amount alone has nothing to be deducted from. refuse_negative: releases exceeding the contracted amount mean the two rows were not the pair this rung assumed.

§2 and §6.4: filings that carry the guarantees only inside the related-party disclosure (关联方担保 / 关联担保), at the AMOUNT UTILISED. Its own rung for the same repeated-disclosure reason as CL_P2 — 关联方担保 is one of the five notes §6.4 names as re-stating the same exposure, so it may substitute for the notes above but never be summed with them.

The related-party disclosure read at the AMOUNT GUARANTEED, when no outstanding balance is printed there. Sits below CL_P4 exactly as CL_P3 sits below CL_P2: §3 ranks the outstanding exposure first, and the guaranteed and utilised figures may never both be counted.

§6.3 last resort. The note's own reported total (Total guarantees / 担保金额合计 / 总担保金额 / 或有负债合计), ALONE in its rung. A filing that itemises no components is the only case where the total is the answer; because no rung may combine the total with components, and rungs are tried in order with the first that resolves winning, the total is reachable only when every rung above it failed — which is precisely "Use 60 and 40 for type totals. Do not calculate 100 + 60 + 40."

items.definition: The cost-of-sales share of the period's depreciation and amortisation, stated as a row whose own caption ties the charge to cost of sales, cost of revenue, cost of goods sold, cost of services or cost of inventories. Because the caption already restricts the figure to the production share, the amount is taken as it stands and nothing is netted off it. It appears among the charges analysed in the note supporting profit or loss before taxation, in the note setting out what profit was arrived at after charging, or in an equivalent analysis of the result from operating activities. It is not that note's unqualified depreciation or amortisation line, which covers every function and is the whole from which this share is carved; it is not the share charged to operating, administrative, selling or distribution expenses; and it is not the profit before tax figure or any of the other charges listed beside it, such as staff costs or auditor's remuneration.

items.prompt: Take only the related-party amount attributable to the current portion of long-term receivables, never the combined total of all non-current assets maturing within one year.

It keeps the shared total veto (合计 / 小计 / total) so it takes the umbrella LINE ITEM and never the note's grand total of receivables plus payables, per 3.5 ('Do not add a subtotal to its components'). It is not the note's grand total, which normally adds receivable and payable balances together, and it is not a subtotal to be taken alongside the same note's class or counterparty rows: where those rows exist they are the measurement and this line is merely their sum. Because a bundled figure can absorb entrusted lending that the note discloses separately, that component is removed from it rather than left inside.
items.prompt: Take the note's one 'due from related parties' line item, never the note's grand total of receivables and payables, and never together with the same note's class or counterparty breakdown.

items.label: Amounts due from related parties note — non-current portion
items.description: Spec 4.4 lists 应收关联方款项 as a related-party note heading in its own right, so this child reads that DEDICATED note — the HK-style 'Amounts due from related companies' note, and the one an English-language filing prints (the parent's definition names exactly this English-alias fallback). Its title is held out of the 关联方及关联交易 group's title so the two never collide. Because the parent is the NON-CURRENT concept (bs_nca), this child claims only the note's non-current-tenor rows by qualifier — non-current portion / 非流动部分 / 一年后到期 / repayable after one year / 长期应收款 — and its veto list restates the shared vetoes plus the mirror-image current qualifiers, so it never picks up the amount belonging to the current-portion concept. The current-portion veto is written as (?:^|\s)current\s+(?:portion|part) and (?:^|[^非])(?:流动部分|流動部分) because a naive veto matches inside 'Non-current portion' and 非流动部分 and would make this child match nothing; both directions are tested.

items.definition: The part of the amounts-due-from-related-parties balance that is repayable after more than one year — the non-current half of that note's tenor split, the amount the filing shows as classified within non-current assets (非流动部分 / 一年后到期 / repayable beyond one year). It is disclosed in a dedicated amounts due from related parties or related companies note (应收关联方款项 / amounts due from related companies), which an English-language filing typically prints in place of the PRC-format class notes. It is not that note's whole balance due from related parties across both tenors, and it is not the portion repayable within one year: the two captions differ only by a qualifier, so a row reading current portion must never be taken here.
items.prompt: Take only the portion repayable after more than one year, never the note's total due from related parties and never the portion due within one year.

items.label: Related-party note — entrusted loans (excluded component)
items.description: Spec 3.4: entrusted loans (委托贷款 / 委托借款 / 委托银行贷款) are excluded from every related-party calculation, and 'If a disclosed total combines entrusted loans with other related-party receivables and the entrusted-loan component cannot be separated, mark the candidate as not computable' — which means that where the component IS disclosed separately it is removed. This child is the FOURTH reader of the 关联方 note and the only one that deliberately overrides the shared veto on those captions, so it matches exactly the rows its three siblings reject; it is trivially disjoint from all of them. It is never a base term: it appears only with role adjustment and sign -1, and only on the two rungs whose base is a single bundled figure. The component-sum rungs (Find_1, Find_2, Find_3A, Find_3B) carry no deduction because the shared veto already keeps entrusted loans out of them, and double-deducting there would be exactly the invented-logic error this configuration avoids. Its own veto list is the shared list with only the five entrusted-loan patterns removed, so payables, totals, movement rows and transaction volumes are still rejected.

items.definition: The separately captioned amount of entrusted lending to a related party (委托贷款 / 委托借款 / 委托银行贷款 / entrusted loans) — funds the entity provides but that a bank advances and administers as its agent, disclosed apart from the entity's own direct related-party receivables. It is disclosed in the related-party relationships and transactions note, as its own row among the related-party balances. It is not a figure this line reports: it exists only to be deducted from a bundled related-party receivable total that absorbs it, so the same lending is not counted inside this line. It is also not an ordinary loan or current-account balance with a related party, and not entrusted borrowing the entity itself owes, which is a liability.
items.prompt: Take only the separately captioned entrusted-loan amount, which serves as a deduction from a bundled related-party figure and is never reported as this line's own value.

items.label: FVTPL current note — note total
items.description: The current-asset FVTPL note (spec 5.1). Reads that note's TOTAL row and nothing else, because spec 5.3 defines Find_1_CP = SUM(unique note_total ...) — so this child deliberately overrides the shared veto on total/合計/合计/總額/总额 and instead vetoes everything a component row could be. This same note is also read by three siblings (included derivatives, included other receivables, non-current split), so it is kept distinguishable by row_caption_any_override matching only total captions and by row_caption_none_override vetoing exactly the qualifiers those siblings own — derivative/衍生, other receivable/其他應收/其他应收, the current and non-current split callouts, level captions — plus class subtotals (listed/unlisted, equity/debt securities, 上市, 股本證券) so a class subtotal is never added to the grand total, and never the note total to its own line items (spec 3.3).

items.definition: The single closing total carrying amount that a note on financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, one figure covering every instrument class the note lists at the reporting date. It is disclosed inside the note headed as financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, financial assets at FVTPL or held-for-trading investments or securities, and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents of those headings. It is not any component row within that note: not a listed or unlisted, quoted or unquoted, equity- or debt-securities class subtotal, not the derivative or other-receivable lines, not a fair-value-level row, and not an opening balance, addition, purchase, disposal, redemption, transfer or exchange-difference movement row. It is also not the balance-sheet face line for securities and other financial assets, and not the total of a different measurement-category note such as the FVTOCI, available-for-sale, held-to-maturity or debt-investments note.
items.prompt: Read only the closing grand total of the FVTPL current-asset note itself, never a class subtotal, component or movement row inside it, and never a total belonging to another measurement-category note.

items.definition: The closing total carrying amount that a note headed with one of the securities names that are current by nature reports at the reporting date, namely investment securities, marketable securities, money market instruments or short-term money market deposits and their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. A filing prints at most one of these as a note heading, and the figure is that note's own total across the securities, funds, bonds, instruments or deposits it lists. It is not an individual security, fund, bond, wealth-management product or deposit row inside the note, and not a listed or unlisted class subtotal. It is also not cash and cash equivalents or bank balances and deposits, which are disclosed in their own note even where a short-term money-market deposit resembles them, and not a total belonging to any of the measurement-category notes.
items.prompt: Take the whole total of the investment, marketable or money-market securities note and never an individual instrument or deposit row inside it, nor any figure from the cash and bank balances note.

items.label: Other financial assets / structured deposits current note — note total
items.description: The residual spec 5.1 headings: 'Other financial assets', the bare 'Financial asset(s)' note, and structured deposits with embedded derivatives (其他金融資產 / 結構性存款 / 含嵌入式衍生工具的結構性存款). The bare form is anchored ^...$ so it cannot swallow the FVTPL, FVTOCI or AFS notes its five siblings own, and 'other financial assets' is matched only as a contiguous phrase so 'Other non-current financial assets' / 其他非流動金融資產 is left to LTP (spec 6.1). One veto had to be narrowed for this child specifically: the total-row veto matches derivatives only at the start of a caption, otherwise 'Total structured deposits with embedded derivatives' — this note's own total — would be vetoed by its own heading.

items.definition: The closing total carrying amount that a residual financial-asset note reports for the holdings it classifies as current assets, disclosed under headings such as other financial assets, a bare financial assets note, or structured deposits including structured deposits with embedded derivatives, together with their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. The figure is the note's own total across the instruments it lists, so where a structured-deposit note totals its deposits inclusive of their embedded derivative element that inclusive total is the amount. It is not the embedded derivative element disclosed as a separate line, nor a wealth-management product, certificate-of-deposit or individual instrument row inside the note. It is also not the total of a note on other non-current financial assets, whose heading contains this one as a substring but which belongs to the long-term field, and not the total of the FVTPL, FVTOCI or debt-investments notes.
items.prompt: Take the other financial assets or structured deposits note's own current-asset total, never a separately disclosed embedded derivative or instrument row inside it, and never a non-current counterpart of the same heading.

items.label: In-scope notes — non-current portion of the note total
items.description: The 'Analysed for reporting purposes as:' non-current callout inside the very notes the six Find_1 children read (note_title_any repeats their six titles verbatim). Spec 5.1 admits only amounts classified under Current Assets and spec 8 requires the classification to match the target field, so where one note total spans both portions the note's own non-current line is removed from it — the deduction is by construction inside the total that was extracted (spec 3.3). Distinguished from the note-total children by row_caption_any_override matching only non-current qualifiers, and every current/non-current veto in both directions is anchored (^current, ^流動, 列作流動 versus non-current, 非流動, 列作非流動) because 'non-current portion' contains 'current portion' as a substring and an unanchored veto would silently kill this child. items.definition: The part of a financial-asset note's total that the note itself states is classified as non-current, shown against a caption such as non-current portion, analysed for reporting purposes as non-current, due after one year, or expected to be recovered or settled more than twelve months after the reporting date, and the Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. It is disclosed as a split-out line inside the very notes whose totals are read for this field, that is the notes on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss or through other comprehensive income, available-for-sale or held-to-maturity financial assets, debt investments, investment and money-market securities, and other financial assets or structured deposits. It is not the current portion of that same split, whose caption differs from it by only one word and which is the part that stays in this field, and it is not the note's own total. Nor is it the total of a separate note on non-current or long-term financial assets, since only an amount sitting inside a total already extracted here may be taken out of it.
items.prompt: Take only the non-current portion that the note carves out of its own total, never the current portion beside it and never the note total itself.

items.label: In-scope current notes — included derivatives (Find_2_CP)
items.description: The first Find_2_CP component, spec 4.2 / 5.2 included_derivatives. note_title_any repeats the six Find_1 note titles verbatim, so a derivative can only be deducted from inside a note whose total was actually extracted — spec 3.3 requires a deduction to be demonstrably included in the extracted note total and forbids deducting a component merely because the term appears elsewhere in the filing. Reads the same notes as the note-total children and is distinguished by row_caption_any_override on derivative captions only (derivative financial instruments, embedded derivatives, forwards, swaps, options, 衍生工具 / 衍生金融工具 / 嵌入式衍生工具 / 遠期外匯合約 / 利率互换). It keeps the shared veto unchanged, total row included, so a 'Total derivatives' subtotal is never added to the derivative rows beneath it; the shared non-current veto also keeps a derivative disclosed as non-current out of this current-portion figure. Optional adjustment, sign -1: spec 5.3 permits Find_2_CP to be zero when the notes were found and no such component sits in their totals.

items.definition: The carrying amount of derivative assets that sits inside the total of a current financial-asset note, shown there under captions such as derivative financial instruments, embedded derivatives, forward foreign exchange contracts, interest rate or cross-currency swaps and option contracts, together with their Traditional and Simplified Chinese equivalents. It is disclosed as a line item within the same notes whose totals are read for this field, so the amount is by construction part of a figure already extracted. It is not that note's own total, and not a derivatives subtotal standing above the individual derivative rows beneath it. It is also not a derivative amount reported anywhere else in the filing, whether a standalone derivative financial instruments note, the balance-sheet face line, a derivative liability, or a derivative shown as non-current, because only a derivative demonstrably included in the extracted total may be deducted from it.
items.prompt: Take a derivative row from inside a note whose total was read, never that note's own total, and never a derivative figure disclosed elsewhere in the filing.

items.label: In-scope current notes — included other receivables (Find_2_CP)
items.description: The second and last Find_2_CP component, spec 4.2 / 5.2 included_other_receivables. Same six note titles as its derivative sibling, for the same inclusion-proof reason (spec 3.3), and distinguished from it by row_caption_any_override on other-receivable captions only (other receivables, 其他應收款項 / 其他應收賬款 / 其他应收款), which share no row with the derivative patterns — checked against the same caption set. Deliberately narrow: spec 4.2 closes with 'The CP field deducts only derivatives and other receivables', so trade receivables and amounts due from related parties are not matched, and no child here deducts investments in related parties, associates or joint ventures — spec 4.2 and 6.3 assign those to LTP alone. It keeps the shared veto, total row included, so a 'Total other receivables' subtotal cannot be added to its own components. Optional adjustment, sign -1 (spec 5.3).

items.definition: The total fair value of financial assets measured using Level 3 inputs, that is significant unobservable inputs, as reported at the reporting date. It is disclosed in the note setting out the fair value hierarchy or fair value measurement of financial instruments, including the Traditional and Simplified Chinese forms of the fair value hierarchy, level and measurement headings. It is not the Level 1 or Level 2 amount, not the hierarchy table's grand total across all three levels, and not the Level 3 total reported in the liabilities half of the same table. Nor is it a row of the Level 3 reconciliation, such as a transfer into or out of Level 3, purchases, issues, settlements or fair-value gains and losses, nor a valuation-technique, unobservable-input or sensitivity narrative row.
items.prompt: Take the Level 3 total for financial assets only, never Level 1 or Level 2, never the table's all-levels grand total or its liabilities column, and never a Level 3 reconciliation movement row.

items.definition: Revenue earned in the period from the entity's principal, ordinary operations, as printed on the face of the income statement itself — the top line, stated before cost of sales and before revenue from any other, non-principal business is added to it. It is read from the consolidated statement of profit or loss, comprehensive income or income statement, and from the group's own statement rather than a parent-company-only one. It is not the wider combined operating revenue total (营业收入, 营业总收入, total revenue), which contains this figure plus other-business revenue; nor is it the cost of sales or gross profit reported next to it, nor a subtotal qualified by product, industry, region or channel.
items.prompt: Take the principal-operations revenue line printed on the face of the consolidated income statement, never the combined operating-revenue total that contains it and never the cost figure reported alongside it.

items.definition: The same principal-operations revenue for the period, read from the dedicated principal-operations line inside the note that analyses operating revenue and operating cost (营业收入, 营业收入和营业成本, Revenue and cost of sales). Because it restates an amount the face may itself report, it is an alternative to the face figure and is never added to it.
items.prompt: Read the principal-operations revenue row inside the operating-revenue note, never that note's combined revenue total and never its cost or margin column.

items.definition: Revenue from ordinary operations for the period as reported in the English or Hong Kong style revenue note — the turnover recognised from contracts with customers that the income statement's top line carries. It is disclosed in a note headed Revenue, Turnover, Revenue from contracts with customers, Disaggregation of revenue, 營業額 or 客户合同收入, and is the route for filings that carry no principal-business and other-business split for a Chinese-language note to supply. It is not the combined revenue-and-other-income total that such a note sometimes heads, and not the other income, other gains, government grant, interest or rental lines disclosed with it. Nor is it one of the disaggregation rows inside the note, which split this very figure by product, market, region or timing of transfer.
items.prompt: Take the note's total revenue from contracts with customers, never a revenue-and-other-income total and never one of the note's disaggregation rows.

items.label: 主营业务分产品 table — product-axis total
items.description: ONE AXIS ONLY — PRODUCT / CATEGORY. An alternative RECONSTRUCTION of the same revenue figure, never a component of it, so it occupies its own cascade rung and is never summed with another axis; a child mixing product and region captions would count the same revenue twice. Reads the axis-qualified TOTAL (分产品…合计, 产品类别小计, 主营业务收入分产品合计, 'revenue by product'), NEVER the individual product rows — §5: do not add a 主营业务 total to its underlying product components. Probed: the component caption 制造业-style product name is claimed by no child. SHARES ITS NOTE with the industry and geography children whenever a filing prints the combined 主营业务分行业、分产品和分地区情况 table, so per the same-note rule its row_caption_any_override identifies its rows by the PRODUCT QUALIFIER in the caption and its row_caption_none_override rejects the 行业 / 业务 / 地区 / 区域 / 渠道 qualifiers; without that the three children would select identical rows, this rung would always fire and the two below it would be unreachable. The shared anchored bare-total veto (`^合计$`) is deliberately left in force, so no axis child can claim an unqualified total — §4.

items.definition: The whole principal-operations revenue figure for the period seen through the product axis — the all-products total that a product analysis carries, which equals the revenue line itself rather than any part of it. It is disclosed in the table analysing revenue by product, product category or product line (主营业务分产品情况, 分产品, revenue by product, product categories). It is not an individual product's or product category's revenue, which is a component of this total and must never stand in for it; it is not the cost, gross profit or proportion-of-revenue column of the same table. It is also not the industry, region or channel total, each of which is a different view of the same revenue and can never be added to this one.
items.prompt: Take the all-products total of the product analysis, never a single product row, never its cost column, and never another axis's total added to it.

items.label: 主营业务分行业 / segment note — industry-axis total
items.description: ONE AXIS ONLY — INDUSTRY / OPERATING SEGMENT / BUSINESS LINE. An alternative reconstruction of the same figure, in its own rung, never summed with another axis. Covers both the PRC 主营业务分行业情况 table and the IFRS segment note (segment information, operating segments, 分部报告, 经营分部资料). Reads the axis-qualified total (分行业…合计, 行业小计, 'segment revenue', 'revenue by segment'), never the individual industry or segment rows — §5 forbids adding a 主营业务 total to its industry components; probed, an industry component caption such as 制造业 is claimed by no child. SHARES ITS NOTE with the product and geography children on the combined 主营业务分行业、分产品和分地区情况 table, so it is identified by the INDUSTRY/SEGMENT QUALIFIER in the caption and vetoes the 产品 / 地区 / 区域 / 渠道 qualifiers — that qualifier split, not the note title, is what keeps the three rungs independently reachable. In a segment note the axis runs across the COLUMNS and this child selects the single 'Revenue' / 分行业 row, leaving the total column to the engine's column selection; the shared vetoes still exclude the segment note's cost, margin, inter-segment and elimination rows.

items.definition: The whole principal-operations revenue figure for the period seen through the industry or operating-segment axis — the all-segments revenue total, which is the revenue line restated by segment and not a share of it. It is disclosed in the table analysing revenue by industry or business line, or in the segment information note, where the revenue row runs across the reportable segments. items.description: ONE AXIS ONLY — GEOGRAPHY / REGION. An alternative reconstruction of the same figure, in its own rung, never summed with another axis. Covers 主营业务分地区情况, 分区域, 地区分部 and the IFRS 'geographical information' / 'revenue by region or market' note. Reads the axis-qualified total (分地区…合计, 地区小计, 'revenue by geographical market'), never the individual country or region rows — §5 forbids adding a 主营业务 total to its geographic components, and 境内 / 境外 style component captions are therefore absent from the override. SHARES ITS NOTE with the product and industry children on the combined 主营业务分行业、分产品和分地区情况 table, so it is identified by the REGION QUALIFIER in the caption and vetoes the 行业 / 业务 / 产品 / 渠道 qualifiers, which is what stops the three axis rungs from collapsing into one figure under three names. The shared anchored bare-total veto stays in force, so an unqualified 合计 in a merged multi-axis table is claimed by nobody.

items.definition: The whole principal-operations revenue figure for the period seen through the geographic axis — the all-regions revenue total, the same revenue restated by location or market. It is disclosed in the table analysing revenue by region or area, or in the geographical information note. It is not one country's, region's or market's revenue, and not a domestic-versus-overseas component of the total. It is also not the non-current assets or other balances that geographical notes commonly disclose by location alongside revenue, and not the product, industry or channel total, which is the same revenue on another axis and never additive with this one.
items.prompt: Take the all-regions revenue total from the geographic analysis, never a single region's revenue, never the non-current assets disclosed by location in the same note, and never another axis's total.

items.description: ONE AXIS ONLY — SALES CHANNEL / SALES MODE (分销售模式, 分渠道, 'revenue by distribution channel'). Last rung, because the spec does not name this axis: §5 names product, industry and geographic components, and this axis is included only as a further alternative reconstruction of the same figure for filings that disaggregate this way. Reads the axis-qualified total (分销售模式…合计, 渠道小计), never the individual 直销 / 经销 channel rows, so §5's ban on adding a total to its components holds here too. Distinguished from the other three axis children by the CHANNEL QUALIFIER in the caption, and vetoes the 行业 / 业务 / 产品 / 地区 / 区域 qualifiers, so if a filing prints all four axes in one table this child still claims only its own rows. Shared vetoes exclude the channel table's cost, margin and 占比 columns.

items.definition: The face amount of letters of credit outstanding at the reporting date — documentary credits, standby credits, and irrevocable or unexpired credits opened on the entity's behalf — carried as an exposure that is not recognised on the balance sheet. It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, including the combined commitments and contingencies heading (或有负债 / 或有事项 / 承诺及或有事项). It is not the note's own total of contingent liabilities or guarantees, it is not the credit facility limit, credit line or undrawn amount the bank has made available, and it is not a movement row such as credits issued, expired or cancelled during the period.
items.prompt: Take only rows whose caption names a letter of credit or a documentary or standby credit, never the note's own total and never a credit facility limit, credit line or undrawn amount.

items.label: Contingency note — performance bonds
items.description: Performance bonds in the same contingency note (§4.3): 履约保函, 履约保证, 履约担保, 合同/工程履约保函. items.definition: The amount of performance bonds and performance guarantees in force at the reporting date — instruments that secure the entity's own performance of a contract or construction obligation (履约保函 / 履约担保 / 履约保证金). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, among the other guarantee instruments listed there. It is not a letter of credit: where a single caption names both instruments, the letter of credit is the more specific reading and owns the row. It is also not a refundable performance deposit paid over and carried as a receivable, which is an asset rather than an exposure, and not the note's own total.
items.prompt: Take only rows whose caption names a performance bond, performance guarantee or 履约保函, never a caption that also names a letter of credit and never a refundable performance deposit held as a receivable.

items.definition: The amount of guarantees a bank has issued on the entity's behalf and that remain in force at the reporting date — payment and advance-payment guarantees, bid and tender guarantees, and financing or non-financing guarantees (银行保函 / 银行保证 / 银行出具的保函). It is not a letter of credit and not a performance bond: both are more specific instruments, and a caption naming either of them belongs to that line rather than here. It is also not the banking facility or credit limit granted, which measures available capacity rather than exposure.
items.prompt: Take only rows whose caption names a bank guarantee or 银行保函, never a caption that also names a letter of credit or performance bond, and never a facility or credit limit.

items.label: Contingency note — corporate guarantees
items.description: Corporate and related-party guarantees in the same contingency note (§4.1): 公司/企业担保, 对外担保, 关联方担保, 为子公司/联营/合营/关联方提供担保, 债务/借款/融资担保, 连带责任保证, 保证责任, and the English "guarantees given in respect of banking facilities granted to subsidiaries" form. It is the broadest label, so it vetoes letters of credit, performance bonds AND bank guarantees — §4.1's explicit sentence plus §5's own two examples (对外担保 + 履约保函 → Performance bonds; 关联方担保 + 银行保函 → Bank guarantees), both verified against these patterns.

items.definition: The amount of guarantees the entity has itself given over another party's obligations — for subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, related parties, customers or suppliers — including joint and several suretyship and guarantees over banking facilities, loans or borrowings granted to those parties (对外担保 / 公司担保 / 企业担保 / 连带责任保证). items.description: The dedicated external-guarantee note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given) read at the AMOUNT UTILISED: 担保余额, 担保责任余额, 实际担保金额, 尚未履行金额, 未结金额, amount utilised / drawn / outstanding. items.definition: The guarantee exposure still outstanding at the reporting date — the portion of the guarantees given that has actually been utilised or drawn down, or the guarantee balance remaining in force at period end (担保余额 / 担保责任余额 / 实际担保金额 / 尚未履行金额 / 未结金额). It is disclosed in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 对外提供担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), where it is printed alongside, and is normally smaller than, the amount guaranteed. It is not that contracted amount guaranteed or guarantee limit, which is a different quantity for the same guarantee and may never be counted with it. It is also not the opening balance of the period and not the note's own aggregate total line.
items.prompt: Take the outstanding or utilised guarantee balance at period end, never the contracted amount guaranteed, never the opening balance and never the note's total.

items.label: Guarantee note — AMOUNT GUARANTEED (contracted)
items.description: The SAME external-guarantee note read at the AMOUNT GUARANTEED: 担保金额, 合同担保金额, 担保限额, amount guaranteed, maximum guarantee / exposure. This is NOT the amount utilised and §3 ranks it below the outstanding exposure, so the two are separate children in separate rungs and are never summed. It therefore VETOES every outstanding-balance caption the balance child owns (担保…余额, 实际担保金额, 尚未履行金额, 未结金额, amount utilised / drawn) — which also stops 实际担保金额 being claimed here through the substring 担保金额. The shared vetoes keep out 授信额度, 合同总额, 累计发生额, 交易金额 and 已确认预计负债, which §3 forbids as the exposure amount, and the 增加/新增 vetoes stop 本期增加担保金额 movement rows.

items.definition: The contracted amount guaranteed — the maximum exposure the guarantee contracts create, whether or not any of it has been drawn (担保金额 / 合同担保金额 / 担保限额 / maximum amount of guarantees). It is disclosed in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 对外提供担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), and it is the figure to use only where that note prints no outstanding guarantee balance. It is not the amount utilised or the outstanding guarantee balance, which is a separate and usually smaller figure for the very same guarantee and must never be added to this one. Nor is it the credit facility or credit limit granted to the borrower, the cumulative amount transacted, or a provision already recognised in respect of the guarantee.
items.prompt: Take the contracted or maximum amount guaranteed, and only where the note prints no outstanding balance — never the utilised or outstanding balance, and never a facility limit or recognised provision.

items.label: Guarantee note — guarantees released or repaid (deduction only)
items.description: The same external-guarantee note's 已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额 / 已归还金额 rows (guarantees released, discharged or repaid in the period). §3 forbids either figure as the exposure amount, so this child is never a figure in its own right: it appears only as the sign -1 adjustment on CL_P3, whose base is the contracted amount guaranteed and which still contains the released and repaid portions. Both other guarantee-note children veto these captions, and this child drops the disposal and released/repaid vetoes it would otherwise self-block on (English repaid/released/discharged/cancelled/terminated, 减少/处置/…, 已偿还/已解除担保/解除担保) while keeping every other shared veto.

items.definition: The amount of guarantees that ceased during the reporting period — guarantees released, discharged, cancelled or terminated, and amounts repaid or returned in the period (已解除担保金额 / 本期解除担保金额 / 已偿还金额 / 已归还金额). It is disclosed as a movement row in the dedicated guarantees-given note (对外担保 / 担保事项 / Guarantees given), and it exists here only to be deducted from the contracted amount guaranteed, which still contains it. It is never a contingent liability in its own right. In particular it is not the outstanding guarantee balance and not the amount guaranteed, and it may not stand in for either.
items.prompt: Take the released, discharged or repaid guarantee row only as a deduction from the contracted amount guaranteed, never as an exposure figure of its own.

items.label: Related-party note — AMOUNT UTILISED (outstanding balance)

items.definition: The contracted amount guaranteed for related parties — the maximum exposure the guarantee contracts create for a parent, subsidiary, associate, joint venture or other related party, whether or not drawn (担保金额 / 合同担保金额 / 担保限额). It is disclosed inside the related-party note (关联方担保 / 关联担保 / 关联方交易), and it is the figure to use only where no outstanding guarantee balance is printed there. It is not the utilised or outstanding balance of the same guarantee, which is a separate figure and may never be counted with it. It is also not the value of related-party transactions for the period and not a loan or current-account balance owed by or to the related party.
items.prompt: Take the contracted amount guaranteed from the related-party note, and only where no outstanding balance appears there — never the utilised balance and never a related-party transaction or loan amount.

items.label: Contingency or guarantee note — the reported total
items.description: The note's own reported TOTAL: Total guarantees / Total contingent liabilities / 担保金额合计 / 担保余额合计 / 总担保金额 / 担保总额 / 或有负债合计. This is the ONE child that deliberately reads a total row, so it is the only one that lifts the shared total vetoes (total, 合计, 总计, 小计) and, with them, the closing-balance vetoes (期末担保余额合计 is a total); every other child keeps them. It sits ALONE in the last cascade rung, which is how §6.3 ("Do not add a reported total to the components included in that total") is made unbreakable rather than merely intended. It still keeps the §3 do-not-use vetoes, so 授信额度合计 or 合同总额 cannot be read as a total exposure.

items.definition: The single aggregate figure the filing itself prints for its contingent exposure — total contingent liabilities, total guarantees, or the guarantee total (担保金额合计 / 担保余额合计 / 担保总额 / 总担保金额 / 或有负债合计). It is disclosed as the total line of the contingent-liabilities, contingencies or guarantees-given note. It is the answer only for a filing that gives this one figure and itemises no instrument types; it may never be counted alongside the classified instrument amounts it already contains. It is also not a total of credit facility limits, contract sums or cumulative transacted amounts, none of which measures exposure.
items.prompt: Take the note's own printed total only where the note itemises no instrument types, and never add it to any type amount it already includes.

items.definition: The amount at stake in a contingency that is not a guarantee instrument — the claim amount, amount in dispute or estimated financial effect of pending litigation and arbitration, legal claims, contract and tax disputes, product warranty obligations, onerous contracts, environmental liabilities and bill or note recourse (涉案金额 / 诉讼金额 / 仲裁金额 / 未决诉讼 / 未决仲裁 / 预计财务影响). It is disclosed inside the contingent liabilities or contingencies note, or in a dedicated litigation and arbitration note (诉讼及仲裁事项 / 重大诉讼、仲裁事项). It is captured as evidence and reported on its own: it is not part of the quantified guarantee and letter-of-credit exposure and must not be summed with those instrument amounts. It is also not a provision already recognised for the same matter (已确认预计负债), which is a recognised liability rather than a contingency.
items.prompt: Capture the claim, disputed or estimated-effect amount of a litigation, arbitration, dispute or warranty matter as separate evidence only, never adding it to the guarantee instrument amounts and never taking a provision already recognised for that matter.

items.label: In-scope financial-asset notes - non-current portion row
items.description: The row a financial-asset note uses to state the part of its own total that is classified as NON-CURRENT: 'Non-current', 'Non-current portion', 'Analysed for reporting purposes as: non-current', 非流動部分, 列作非流動資產. Spec 6.1 - 'Only use amounts classified under Non-current Assets for this field' - names this row rather than the note's combined total wherever a note covers both halves, which is why this child owns the first cascade rung. Its note titles are the whole in-scope dictionary of 6.1, so it reads the same notes as children 2-9; it is distinguished from them by REQUIRING the non-current qualifier in the caption (row_caption_any_override), which nothing in the shared total vocabulary matches, and the shared vetoes drop the matching current-portion row so the current half can never land on this line. One figure per note: this row or the note's combined total, never both (spec 3.3).

items.definition: The part of a financial-asset note's own carrying amount that the note itself states is classified as non-current, taken from the row that carries the non-current qualifier: Non-current, Non-current portion, Analysed for reporting purposes as non-current, amounts due after more than one year, 非流動部分, 列作非流動. It is disclosed inside the notes that analyse securities and other financial assets, whatever heading a filing uses for them, including financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income, available-for-sale or held-to-maturity financial assets, debt investments, other financial assets, investment securities or securities investments, and structured deposits, and their 金融資產 / 金融资产 equivalents. It is not the note's combined total where the note covers both halves of the balance, and it is not the current-portion row printed beside it; where a note analyses itself into current and non-current, only the amount the note assigns to non-current belongs here.
items.prompt: Take the row a financial-asset note labels as non-current, never that note's combined current-plus-non-current total and never the current-portion row sitting next to it.

items.definition: The total carrying amount of the note that analyses financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss, read once from that note's own total or carrying-amount line, in the case where the whole note is classified as non-current and prints no current/non-current split. It is disclosed in the note headed financial assets at fair value through profit or loss or FVTPL, and in Chinese under 按公平值計入損益的金融資產 or 以公允價值計量且其變動計入當期損益的金融資產 and their simplified forms. It is not one of the instrument sub-lines the note itemises beneath that total, such as listed or unlisted equity securities, funds, wealth-management products or debt instruments, and it is not a cost, gross amount, impairment, fair-value-movement or fair-value-hierarchy line. Where the note does state a separate non-current portion, that stated portion is the figure and this combined total is not.
items.prompt: Take the fair-value-through-profit-or-loss note's own total once, never an instrument sub-line beneath it and never this total when the note itself states a separate non-current portion.

items.definition: The total carrying amount of a note whose heading is simply financial assets, or non-current financial assets, read once from that note's own total or carrying-amount line, where the note is wholly non-current and prints no current/non-current split. items.definition: The amount at which the non-trade receivables class is carried after its loss allowance has already been deducted, stated by the note as a net figure — a row captioned net carrying amount, net book value, net amount, 账面价值 or 净额, or the class name qualified as net of loss allowance or net of impairment. It is disclosed inside the note dealing with other receivables, non-trade or sundry receivables, or the combined deposits, prepayments and other receivables disclosure. It is not the gross closing balance of the same class before any allowance, not the loss allowance or bad-debt provision row, and not the related-party amount reported inside that same note; those are three separate figures standing beside it. It is also not the prepayments or deposits that may share the note's title but are not other receivables.
items.prompt: Take only the row this note itself presents as already net of the loss allowance, never the gross closing balance, the allowance row, or a related-party sub-line inside the same note.

items.label: Other receivables note — gross closing balance
items.description: The gross book balance of other receivables, used only by the fallback rung: spec 3.2 preference 2, closing balance less loss allowance. It shares the note with three siblings and is identified by the GROSS qualifier — 账面余额 / 期末余额 / closing balance / gross carrying amount / 其他应收款合计. Because that class-labelled closing total IS what this child is deliberately reading, its override lifts the family's closing-balance veto and the trailing-total veto, and this is why. It still vetoes the BARE 合计 / 小计 / total row (which repeats in every sub-table of the note and would otherwise be summed several times), 期初余额 / opening balance, 账面原值, the net markers owned by sub__cp_other_receivables_net, the allowance owned by sub__cp_other_receivables_loss_allowance, and every related-party caption owned by sub__cp_other_receivables_rp. Because the bare-total risk cannot be fully closed by caption text alone, this child feeds the FALLBACK rung only, never the primary one.

items.definition: The book balance of the non-trade receivables class at the reporting date before any loss allowance is taken off — the gross or closing carrying amount of the class, captioned as gross carrying amount, closing balance, total other receivables, 账面余额 or 期末余额 of that class. It is disclosed in the note dealing with other receivables, non-trade receivables, or the combined deposits, prepayments and other receivables disclosure. It is not the net carrying amount of the same class, which is this balance less the allowance, and it is not the allowance itself; nor is it the opening balance, the original cost 账面原值, or the unlabelled total of an ageing, largest-debtor or movement sub-table that repeats inside the note. Only a balance the note labels as the closing gross amount of the other-receivables class counts.
items.prompt: Take the class's own gross closing balance before the allowance, never the net figure printed beside it and never a bare total line belonging to an ageing, debtor-concentration or movement sub-table.

items.label: Other receivables note — loss allowance / bad-debt provision
items.description: The loss allowance disclosed in the other-receivables note — 坏账准备 / 信用损失准备 / 信用减值准备 / 损失准备 / 减值准备 / 壞賬準備 / loss allowance / allowance for expected credit losses / provision for impairment. This is a NEGATIVE row and it is deliberately CLAIMED, not vetoed: it is the only child that overrides the family's allowance veto, and it enters the parent cascade as an adjustment term with sign -1 so that gross less allowance equals the net carrying amount the spec requires (3.2 preference 2). Vetoing it instead would overstate the line. It still vetoes the allowance ROLL-FORWARD rows — 本期计提 / 核销 / 转回 / 收回 / additions / written off — and the accumulated forms and the roll-forward's own 期初余额 / 期末余额, so only the balance-sheet-date allowance is taken and the movement is never double counted. It also vetoes the net and gross markers owned by its two siblings and every related-party caption.

items.definition: The loss allowance, bad-debt provision, credit-loss or impairment provision standing against the non-trade receivables class at the reporting date — 坏账准备, 信用损失准备, 损失准备 or their English equivalents — which is a deduction from those receivables and not a receivable itself. It appears in the note dealing with other receivables, non-trade receivables, or the combined deposits, prepayments and other receivables disclosure, typically as a less-prefixed line sitting between the gross balance and the net one. It is not the gross balance it is deducted from, and it is not the net amount left after deducting it. It is also not a movement in the allowance — the amount provided, written off, recovered or reversed during the period — nor an allowance roll-forward's opening or accumulated column; only the provision standing at the reporting date counts.
items.prompt: Take the allowance standing against these receivables at the reporting date, never the gross or net balance it sits between, and never the period's charge, write-off, recovery or reversal.

items.label: Current portion of long-term receivables note — net amount
items.description: current_long_term_receivables_net. Reads the 一年内到期的非流动资产 / 长期应收款 note. Its note can be an OMNIBUS note that also lists sibling classes (一年内到期的贷款及垫款 and other maturing non-current assets), so it carries a narrowed row_caption_any_override limited to the 一年内到期的长期应收款 caption — that is what stops it re-claiming a row another child already owns, and it enforces spec 4.2's rule that when 一年内到期的非流动资产 is a combined total only the component explicitly attributable to 一年内到期的长期应收款 may be used. The family veto anchors out the combined 一年内到期的非流动资产 caption, the bare 长期应收款 caption and every 非流动 / over-one-year row, so no non-current amount reaches the current pool. Related-party rows in this same note belong to sub__cp_current_ltr_rp and are vetoed here.
