items.definition: The portion of long-term receivables falling due within one year of the reporting date, at its carrying amount after any allowance against it — a receivable reclassified out of non-current assets into the current pool solely because of its maturity. It is disclosed in the note dealing with long-term receivables, or with non-current assets maturing within one year, which is where a filing sets the maturing slice out from the rest of the class. It is not the whole long-term receivables balance, and not the part still falling due after more than one year; it is also not the combined total of all non-current assets maturing within one year, which can additionally contain maturing loans and advances and other maturing classes that are extracted separately. Related-party amounts disclosed in the same note are a separate figure and not part of this one.
items.prompt: Take only the slice of long-term receivables maturing within one year, never the full long-term balance and never the combined maturing-non-current-assets total that surrounds it.

items.label: Other receivables note — related-party amount included
items.description: other_receivables_related_party_net — the deduction leg for the other-receivables component. It shares its note with three siblings and is separated from them by the RELATED-PARTY qualifier alone: 关联方 / 关联单位 / 关联企业 / 关联公司 / 母公司 / 子公司 / 联营企业 / 合营企业 / 受同一控制方控制的企业 / 应收关联方款项 / 关联方组合 / due from related parties — exactly the spec 3.3 identification list, so related-party status is never inferred from a counterparty name. Overriding the family's related-party veto is the whole point of this child. Its own veto adds the spec 4.4 exclusions: 应付关联方款项 and other due-TO balances, 预收款项, 合同负债, related-party investments, 担保金额, and transaction volumes with no outstanding balance. It also vetoes the pooled allowance, because spec 4.3 forbids allocating a pooled allowance to related parties. Enters the cascade with sign -1 and only ever deducts an amount read from the same note that supplied the gross component, which is what makes it proven-included (spec 5.3).

items.definition: The part of the non-trade receivables class that is owed by related parties — parents, subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, fellow subsidiaries, controlling shareholders and other counterparties the filing itself identifies as related — read from the same note that discloses the class. It exists so that a related-party amount already sitting inside the other-receivables balance can be carved back out of a third-party line. It is not the class total that contains it, and it is not the entity's own balances payable to related parties, advances received or contract liabilities on the other side of the balance sheet. It is also not a related-party transaction volume, turnover or guarantee amount with no receivable outstanding at the reporting date, and not a share of the class's pooled allowance.
items.prompt: Take only the receivable balance this note attributes to related parties inside the other-receivables class, never the class total, never a due-to-related-party amount, and never a transaction or guarantee volume.

items.label: Current portion of long-term receivables note — related-party amount included
items.description: current_long_term_receivables_related_party_net. The same related-party vocabulary read from the 一年内到期的非流动资产 / 长期应收款 note, and separated from sub__cp_current_ltr_net — which reads that same note — by the related-party qualifier alone. Its veto blocks the bare 长期应收款 caption and every 非流动 / over-one-year row, so this deduction can only carry an amount classified as 一年内到期的长期应收款: spec 5.3 forbids deducting 长期应收款 that is not in the CP gross pool. Sign -1.

items.definition: The part of the long-term receivables maturing within one year that is owed by related parties, as that note identifies them. It is read from the note dealing with long-term receivables or with non-current assets maturing within one year — the same note that discloses the maturing slice itself — so the related-party amount can be carved out of a line that would otherwise be third-party only. It is not related-party long-term receivables still falling due after more than one year, which never entered the current pool and so must not be deducted from it. It is also not the whole maturing slice, and not an amount payable to a related party.
items.prompt: Deduct only the related-party amount inside the within-one-year slice of long-term receivables, never a related-party long-term balance maturing later and never the whole slice.

items.label: Loans and advances note — related-party current-portion amount included
items.description: current_loans_and_advances_related_party_net. Related-party rows inside the 发放贷款及垫款 note, separated from sub__cp_current_loans_advances_net by the related-party qualifier. Its veto blocks the bare and the non-current loans-and-advances captions, so non-current loans and advances are never deducted (spec 5.3). Note that 委托贷款 / entrusted loans are deliberately NOT vetoed here: spec 5.3 states the LTP entrusted-loan exclusion does not carry over to this field, so a related-party entrusted loan sitting inside the CP gross pool is deducted like any other related-party amount. Sign -1.

items.definition: The part of the loans and advances maturing within one year that is owed by related-party borrowers, as the note identifies them. It is read from the note dealing with loans and advances or with their current portion — the same note that supplies the current-portion figure — which is what shows the amount is already inside the balance being reduced. It is not related-party lending falling due after more than one year, which lies outside the current pool and must not be deducted from it, and it is not the whole current portion. Entrusted or on-lent arrangements to a related party do belong here when that balance sits within the current portion.
items.prompt: Deduct only the related-party share of loans and advances maturing within one year, never a related-party loan due after one year and never the whole current portion.

items.definition: The part of the interbank placement balance that is placed with a related institution — a parent, a fellow subsidiary, an associate or another counterparty the filing identifies as related. It is read from the same placements-with-banks or funds-placed note that supplies the placement figure, since only an amount shown inside that balance can be carved out of it. It is not the whole placement balance, and it is not funds taken in from a related institution, which is a liability rather than a receivable. It is also not a related-party placement mentioned only as a transaction elsewhere without being shown inside this class at the reporting date.
items.prompt: Deduct only the related-party placement shown inside this note, never the note's whole placement balance and never funds the entity has taken in from a related institution.

items.definition: The part of the current-account receivable balance that is due from related parties — intra-group and other related-unit running accounts, 关联方往来款 and its variants — as the filing identifies them. It is read from the same current-account or other current assets note that supplies the current-account figure, since only an amount shown inside that balance can be carved out of it. It is not the whole current-account balance, and it is not a current account the entity owes to a related party, which sits on the liability side. It is also not the related-party transaction turnover for the period; only the balance outstanding at the reporting date counts.
items.prompt: Deduct only the related-party balance shown inside this current-account receivable, never the whole current-account figure and never an amount the entity owes a related party.
